primary_sources.access_scope: The selected cache remains abstract-only. Authentic indexed original Results/Methods were inspected separately: a human brain-library screen preceded mechanistic assays using rat MAGUIN-1 668–1032 with human Densin/PSD-95. Tail deletion, self-association-region deletion and absence-of-MAGUIN controls establish ternary assembly; dimer versus multimer is unresolved. The positive MINT pair has a Densin-region mapping discrepancy relative to the primary negative control; the underlying positive experiment remains valid.

The complete authentic abstract and a separately recovered original first-page excerpt support the positive human CNK2 findings. Complete Methods/Results were not recovered after bounded attempts. Detailed phosphorylation mechanism, native stoichiometry and full construct equivalence are not inferred.

The main-selected abstract is preserved. Genuine fresh normal full text was inspected separately, including human CNK2 5–84/fly HYP 21–98 recombinant Methods, binding and structural Results. Functional S2 signaling assays use fly proteins; human 2–485 plus fly HYP does not bind fly KSR in the reported assay.

The original abstract and authentic laboratory database target row/header/reference key were read. CNKSR2/NP_055742 is listed with two peptides under this study in healthy-human urinary exosomes. Complete original Methods were not recovered or claimed read; earlier challenge/error responses are excluded.

Selected complete human-library Methods and CNK2-specific Results were inspected in the genuine full cache. Both MaMTH and tagged coimmunoprecipitation support the EGFR pair, including wild-type EGFR. Later cancer/mechanistic experiments focus on TACC3 and are not transferred.

Selected complete holdup Methods, affinity Results and fragment-versus-full-protein discussion were read. Exact target/partner domain coordinates, tags, positive flags and record identifiers are preserved separately. These are peptide/domain measurements, not native full-length complex demonstrations.

Selected complete mouse genetic, construct, biochemical, imaging and electrophysiological Methods/Results were read. MAGUIN-1/-2 constructs are mouse, with rat afadin constructs in HEK293 cells. PSD-95/AMPA clustering changes are distinguished from unchanged cluster density, total surface receptor abundance and seizure findings.

Selected complete Methods/Results were read. Constructs are mouse Cnk2A/B and deletions, tested in heterologous cells and rat hippocampal neurons; endogenous rat localization was also assayed. ΔPH-mediated TNIK redistribution is distinct from the nonsignificant knockdown effect on dendritic TNIK and unresolved causal link to PSD size.

Selected complete Results and available Methods were read, including rat hippocampal neuron rescue/mutation experiments and NG108 biochemical assays. The isolated CNK2 Vilse-binding region does not alter Vilse GAP activity; cellular binding disruption instead changes localization and Rac-GTP readouts. No full supplementary Methods or all-product equivalence is claimed.

The complete authentic abstract explicitly reports neuronal cell-body/neurite localization, membrane association, terminal PDZ binding and rat-brain coimmunoprecipitation. Full Methods and figures were not recovered; the source is used only for those positive bounded findings.

The original abstract and exact current mouse donor GOA relationship were inspected, but the CNKSR2-specific phosphoproteomic target table was not recovered. The publication is not judged invalid or miscited. Independent neuronal sources support the reviewed postsynaptic-density location.

terms.name: postsynaptic density
terms.definition: An electron dense network of proteins within and adjacent to the postsynaptic membrane of an asymmetric, neuron-neuron synapse. Its major components include neurotransmitter receptors and the proteins that spatially and functionally organize them such as anchoring and scaffolding molecules, signaling enzymes and cytoskeletal components.

terms.name: GTPase binding
terms.definition: Binding to a GTPase, any enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of GTP.

terms.name: membrane
terms.definition: A lipid bilayer along with all the proteins and protein complexes embedded in it and attached to it.

terms.name: protein-macromolecule adaptor activity
terms.definition: An adaptor activity that brings together two or more macromolecules in contact, permitting those molecules to function in a coordinated way. The adaptor can bring together two proteins, or a protein and another macromolecule such as a lipid or a nucleic acid.
terms.comment: Note that protein complex scaffolds should use GO:0140378 protein complex scaffold activity.

terms.name: PDZ domain binding
terms.definition: Binding to a PDZ domain of a protein, a domain found in diverse signaling proteins.

terms.name: signaling receptor complex adaptor activity
terms.definition: The binding activity of a molecule that provides a physical support for the assembly of a multiprotein receptor signaling complex.

terms.name: cytoplasm
terms.definition: The contents of a cell excluding the plasma membrane and nucleus, but including other subcellular structures.

terms.name: plasma membrane
terms.definition: The membrane surrounding a cell that separates the cell from its external environment. It consists of a phospholipid bilayer and associated proteins.

terms.name: identical protein binding
terms.definition: Binding to an identical protein or proteins.

terms.name: protein homodimerization activity
terms.definition: Binding to an identical protein to form a homodimer.

terms.name: protein binding
terms.definition: Binding to a protein.

terms.name: signaling receptor binding
terms.definition: Binding to one or more specific sites on a receptor molecule, a macromolecule that undergoes combination with a hormone, neurotransmitter, drug or intracellular messenger to initiate a change in cell function.
terms.comment: Where appropriate, also consider annotating to 'receptor agonist activity ; GO:0048018'.

terms.name: actin cytoskeleton organization
terms.definition: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of cytoskeletal structures comprising actin filaments and their associated proteins.

terms.name: protein kinase binding
terms.definition: Binding to a protein kinase, any enzyme that catalyzes the transfer of a phosphate group, usually from ATP, to a protein substrate.

terms.name: protein domain specific binding
terms.definition: Binding to a specific domain of a protein.

terms.name: protein phosphatase binding
terms.definition: Binding to a protein phosphatase.

terms.name: protein-membrane adaptor activity
terms.definition: The binding activity of a molecule that brings together a protein or a protein complex with a membrane, either via membrane lipid binding or by interacting with a membrane protein, to establish or maintain the localization of the protein, protein complex or organelle.

terms.name: postsynaptic specialization organization
terms.definition: A process that results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a postsynaptic specialization, a structure that lies adjacent to the cytoplasmic face of the postsynaptic membrane.

terms.name: extrinsic component of postsynaptic density membrane
terms.definition: The component of the postsynaptic density membrane consisting of gene products and protein complexes that are loosely bound to one of its surfaces, but not integrated into the hydrophobic region.

terms.name: postsynapse organization
terms.definition: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a postsynapse.

terms.name: scaffold protein binding
terms.definition: Binding to a scaffold protein. Scaffold proteins are crucial regulators of many key signaling pathways. Although not strictly defined in function, they are known to interact and/or bind with multiple members of a signaling pathway, tethering them into complexes.

terms.name: postsynaptic membrane
terms.definition: A specialized area of membrane facing the presynaptic membrane on the tip of the nerve ending and separated from it by a minute cleft (the synaptic cleft). Neurotransmitters cross the synaptic cleft and transmit the signal to the postsynaptic membrane.

terms.name: intracellular signal transduction
terms.definition: The process in which a signal is passed on to downstream components within the cell, which become activated themselves to further propagate the signal and finally trigger a change in the function or state of the cell.

terms.name: signaling adaptor activity
terms.definition: The binding activity of a molecule that brings together two or more molecules in a signaling pathway, permitting those molecules to function in a coordinated way. Adaptor molecules themselves do not have catalytic activity.
terms.comment: A signaling adaptor can bring together both protein and non-protein molecules within a signaling pathway. Scaffold proteins act in at least four ways: tethering signaling components, localizing these components to specific areas of the cell, regulating signal transduction by coordinating positive and negative feedback signals, and insulating correct signaling proteins from competing proteins (PMID:19104498).

terms.name: extracellular exosome
terms.definition: A vesicle that is released into the extracellular region by fusion of the limiting endosomal membrane of a multivesicular body with the plasma membrane. Extracellular exosomes, also simply called exosomes, have a diameter of about 40-100 nm.

terms.name: cytoskeletal protein binding
terms.definition: Binding to a protein component of a cytoskeleton (actin, microtubule, or intermediate filament cytoskeleton).

terms.name: glutamatergic synapse
terms.definition: A synapse that uses glutamate as a neurotransmitter.

terms.name: transcription coregulator binding
terms.definition: Binding to a transcription coregulator, a protein involved in regulation of transcription via protein-protein interactions with transcription factors and other transcription regulatory proteins. Cofactors do not bind DNA directly, but rather mediate protein-protein interactions between regulatory transcription factors and the basal transcription machinery.

terms.name: neuronal cell body
terms.definition: The portion of a neuron that includes the nucleus, but excludes cell projections such as axons and dendrites.
terms.comment: Note that 'cell body' and 'cell soma' are not used in the literature for cells that lack projections, nor for some cells (e.g. yeast with mating projections) that do have projections.

terms.name: protein serine/threonine kinase binding
terms.definition: Binding to a protein serine/threonine kinase.

terms.name: enzyme-linked receptor protein signaling pathway
terms.definition: The series of molecular signals initiated by an extracellular ligand binding to a receptor on the surface of the target cell, where the receptor possesses catalytic activity or is closely associated with an enzyme such as a protein kinase, and ending with the regulation of a downstream cellular process, e.g. transcription.

terms.name: regulation of signal transduction
terms.definition: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of signal transduction.

terms.name: protein heterodimerization activity
terms.definition: Binding to a nonidentical protein to form a heterodimer.

terms.name: epidermal growth factor receptor binding
terms.definition: Binding to an epidermal growth factor receptor.

terms.name: protein complex scaffold activity
terms.definition: A structural molecule activity of a protein-containing complex component that serves to hold the complex together. Protein complex scaffolds are integral members of complexes.

terms.name: ubiquitin ligase complex scaffold activity
terms.definition: The binding activity of a molecule that brings together an ubiquitin ligase and an ubiquitin ligase-substrate adaptor, permitting those molecules to function in a coordinated way.

terms.name: MAP kinase scaffold activity
terms.definition: The binding activity of a molecule that functions as a physical support for the assembly of a multiprotein mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) complex. Binds multiple kinases of the MAPKKK cascade, and also upstream signaling proteins, permitting those molecules to function in a coordinated way. Bringing together multiple enzymes and their substrates enables the signal to be transduced quickly and efficiently.

terms.name: centriole scaffold activity
terms.definition: The binding activity of a protein that contributes to the stable formation of a centriole by forming persistent structures, or templates, upon which other centriolar proteins assemble.
